context: Alma is about to eat a meal the speaker has good grounds for thinking she will enjoy: she enjoyed it when the speaker prepared it before, the speaker has sampled it, and it tastes good.
comment: Assertible on prior inferential grounds; Cumming's version of Ninan's case.

context: The next day, with only the prior inferential grounds of (1).
comment: Asserting it would suggest further, post-prandial grounds. (2) is printed without a judgment mark; the infelicity on prior inferential grounds is stated in prose ('Can I now assert the following...? It seems not.').

context: Alma told the speaker after the meal that she enjoyed it.
comment: Hearsay causally downstream of the event; direct witnessing and the empty plate are the paper's other downstream grounds.

primaryText: Alma will have enjoyed the meal.
context: The next day, with only the prior inferential grounds of (1).
comment: Felicitous though the grounds have not changed since (1).

primaryText: Alma will be enjoying the meal (right now).
comment: The constraint is absent when the future form speaks about the present; the scenario, during the meal on the prior inferential grounds of (1), is reconstructed.

primaryText: Alma is enjoying the meal (right now).
comment: Ninan's observation that present-tense sentences too cannot be asserted on prior inferential grounds; the scenario, during the meal on the prior inferential grounds of (1), is reconstructed. (12b) is printed without a judgment mark in the list (12); the infelicity on prior inferential grounds is stated in prose, citing Ninan (2022, p. 406).

primaryText: The Fed will have raised interest rates at today's meeting.
comment: Felicitous only with a non-abductive inferential justification; the scenario, after the meeting on economic indicators known beforehand, is reconstructed from (3a).

primaryText: The Fed will have raised interest rates at today's meeting.
context: After the meeting, having just read in the evening paper that the rates were raised.
comment: No good on evidence causally downstream of the meeting. (21a) is printed without a judgment mark; the prose says it 'is no good if you have just read in the evening paper that the rates were raised'.

translation: [I made a sensory observation that] it was raining.
context: Yenghi saw it raining yesterday; now she says.
comment: Present tense under -te: the sensory evidence is contemporaneous with the event.

translation: [I inferred (from the acquired sensory evidence) that] it had rained.
context: Yenghi saw yesterday that the ground was wet; now she says.
comment: Past tense under -te: the event precedes the sensory evidence.

translation: [I inferred (from the acquired sensory evidence) that] it would rain.
context: Yenghi saw the overcast sky yesterday; now she says.
comment: Future tense under -te: forward-looking inferential evidence for an event that has since come and gone.

translation: [I see that] it is raining now.
context: Chelswu sees it raining now and says.
comment: Under -ney the sensory evidence is present, so the present tense settles both perspectives.

translation: [I infer that] it rained a minute ago.
context: Chelswu sees the wet ground now and says.
comment: Past tense under -ney: the event precedes the present sensory evidence.

translation: [I infer that] it will rain tonight.
context: Chelswu sees the cloudy sky now and says.
comment: Future tense under -ney: present evidence that is prospective is for a future event.

translation: Yesterday, it rained in Paris, I inferred/heard.
context: You learned earlier today that it had rained yesterday in Paris.
comment: Nonfuture under -l: the evidence is downstream of the event. Cumming prints Pariz; Koev (2017) prints Pariž, the standard transliteration.

primaryText: Včera v Pariž štja-l-o da vali.
translation: Yesterday, it rained in Paris, I inferred/heard.
context: You learned earlier today that it had rained yesterday in Paris.
comment: Future under -l requires prospective evidence, which the scenario lacks. Cumming prints Pariz; Koev (2017) prints Pariž, the standard transliteration.

primaryText: Včera v Pariž štja-l-o da vali.
translation: Yesterday, it was going to rain in Paris, I inferred/heard.
context: The day before yesterday you watched the weather forecast and learned that it was going to rain yesterday in Paris.
comment: The future appears on a sentence describing an event in the past. Cumming prints Pariz; Koev (2017) prints Pariž, the standard transliteration.

translation: Yesterday, it was going to rain in Paris, I inferred/heard.
context: The day before yesterday you watched the weather forecast and learned that it was going to rain yesterday in Paris.
comment: Nonfuture under -l requires downstream evidence, which a forecast is not. Cumming prints Pariz; Koev (2017) prints Pariž, the standard transliteration.

translation: Tomorrow it rains in Sofia, I gather.
comment: Nonfuture evidential sentences are restricted to events in the present or past of speech time; the acquisition time is stipulated at speech.

translation: Tomorrow he is in Sofia, I gather.
context: The speaker knows only of the plan.
comment: A planned event is exempt from both the utterance and the evidential perspective of the nonfuture evidential.

translation: [I inferred (from the acquired sensory evidence) that] Obama is coming to Korea next week.
context: Yenghi read the newspaper yesterday, which mentioned Obama's visit to Korea next week; now she says.
comment: A scheduled event that the speaker has not witnessed takes the present tense under -te. Cumming prints nayewu-ey; Lee (2013) prints naycwu-ey (Yale romanization of 'next week'). Lee's translation reads 'Obama comes to Korea next week'.

primaryText: He's great. He spent the weekend in New York.
context: Jack told the speaker on Thursday that he was leaving the next day for a weekend in New York; on Monday, without having heard from him, the speaker is asked how Jack is doing.
comment: A planned event exempt from the downstream requirement of the simple past.

context: At 1 p.m. Simona told Akari she would be at the library at 2 p.m. to return some books; at 2:30 p.m. Jess asks Akari whether the books were returned.
comment: A scheduled event exempt from the downstream requirement of the simple past.

primaryText: Alma is enjoying the meal tonight.
comment: The present tense normally requires the event to overlap the present; the acquisition time is stipulated at speech. Expands the starred variant of the printed (30) 'Alma is enjoying the meal (right now/*tonight).'

primaryText: Jack is spending next weekend in New York.
context: The scenario of (28).
comment: The futurate present: a planned future event described with the present tense.

primaryText: Simona is returning the books later today.
context: The scenario of (29).
comment: The futurate present: a scheduled event described with the present tense.
